raj: Quick follow-up from the FP8/INT8/INT4 attention RFC — I ran a small smoke plan across 4 nodes and hit a couple unexpected regressions.
raj: TL;DR: fused dequant-after-attn gives big wins on long seqs but hurts 1-16 token latency in some kernels.
maria: thanks for running this — do you have a minimal repro or a log capture?
raj: yes, pasted below. repro is the 1-shot chat workload with batch=1, seq=8, model=redwood-7B-q8.
raj: log snippet:
```
[2026-02-20 13:12:31.112] kernel_selector: picked fused_dequant_attn_q8 for layer 12
[2026-02-20 13:12:31.119] runtime: kv-cache miss -> fallback to unfused path
[2026-02-20 13:12:31.135] latency_ms: unfused=12.3 fused=21.7
```
kevin: interesting. sounds like the fused kernel has a higher setup overhead that dominates on short seqs.
kevin: also possible we hit poor launch config (blocks/warps) on Ampere-ish cards for small N.
tess: did you try the runtime flag experimental.dequant_fuse_latency_threshold?
raj: yeah set to 32 and it flips to unfused for seq<32 which helped. but that's a magic number; we need a principled selector.
maria: agreed — we should add a selector heuristic that accounts for seq_len, batch_size, qtype, and warm/cache state.
raj: proposal (pseudo):
```
score = base_perf(qtype,kernel) - setup_cost(kernel)/max(1,seq_len) + cache_hit_bonus
choose kernel with max(score)
```
kevin: i like the mathy approach. we have base_perf tables per kernel from microbenchmarks already.
kevin: only missing is a cheap runtime estimate for setup_cost and cache_hit probability.
tess: cache_hit_prob could be estimated from request metadata: if request.prefetch==true or request.kv_prefetched==true then high.
maria: can we instrument the runtime to record per-route empirical breakpoints and feed them into the selector? e.g., after N requests recompute thresholds.
raj: yes — online learning. but keep it bounded: only adapt when we have >=1000 samples per route and persist policy to control plane.
raj: edge-case: INT4 fused path currently uses different packing layout. there is a compatibility hazard when falling back between kernels mid-inference.
kevin: that's important. if we switch kernels and the KV layout differs, we must either rewrite the cache or disallow mid-session switches.
tess: option A: maintain unified KV layout interface and add thin shims for kernel-specific packing/unpacking (costly).
kevin: option B: pin kernel per-session (simpler), migrate on model version/rollout boundaries.
maria: i'd prefer B for correctness. pin kernel for the life of a conversation; use routing policy to change kernel for new sessions only.
raj: pin-per-session + selector pre-check on session start sounds safe. for stateless batched requests we can keep dynamic selection.
infra-bot: deploybot: canary rollout scheduled for fused_dequant_attn v2 on infra-prod-4 at 2026-02-21T02:00Z :robot_face:
kevin: one more perf nit: FP8 fused path exposes more register pressure; on Turing-era cards it spills and loses throughput. need a kernel tag for hw_capability.
maria: add hw_tags to kernel metadata: {arch_min, reg_pressure_est, shared_mem_bytes}. selector can filter unsupported hw or penalize heavy reg_pressure.
raj: action items:
- kevin: add reg_pressure and setup_cost metrics to kernel metadata (ETA 2d)
- tess: implement seq-aware selector heuristic + session pinning (ETA 3d)
- maria: add per-route telemetry + persistence hook to control plane (ETA 5d)
- raj: run extended smoke plan across gen1/gen2 GPUs and post results (ETA 3d)
kevin: I'll prototype a tiny table-based selector in the runtime to validate heuristics before full ML-based adaptation.
tess: I'll add a feature flag: runtime.quant_selector_mode = {static, heuristic, adaptive}
maria: + add infra metrics dashboard: selector decisions, perf delta, cache hits.
raj: thanks all. if we agree on session pinning I'll update the RFC with the selector rules and KV layout compatibility note.
maria: +1. also add an explicit incompatibility matrix for INT4 packing variants so SRE and ops know migration caveats.
kevin: FYI I'll dump microbenchmarks in gist and link.
raj: awesome. linking results here when done. :thumbsup:
